propositions.proposition: AI-assisted educational work necessarily reduces learning.
propositions.resolution: AI use must be separated by interaction design. A structured AI pre-lecture scaffold produced learning outcomes comparable to human pre-lecture interaction in Peng et al. (2026), so evidence does not support treating every AI-assisted condition as cognitive substitution.

propositions.proposition: Lower neural connectivity or activation during AI use proves lower cognitive ability.
propositions.resolution: Neural engagement/connectivity and cognitive ability are distinct constructs. Methodological critique of Kosmyna et al. and the Frontiers theory review both require conservative interpretation.

propositions.proposition: The Kosmyna et al. essay-writing experiment establishes durable generalized cognitive decline from LLM use.
propositions.resolution: The experiment is task-bounded, session 4 is small and optional, the institutional page calls for longitudinal work, and a methodological comment raises design/EEG/reproducibility concerns. Durable generalized capability remains unresolved.

propositions.proposition: AI can function as a learning scaffold rather than a substitute.
propositions.resolution: Peng et al. provide experimental evidence that a structured AI pre-lecture interaction can improve learning and neural alignment relative to no interaction. This does not establish all scaffolding designs as beneficial, but it validates scaffold-versus-substitute as an empirically meaningful distinction.

propositions.proposition: Unobserved cognitive substitution is an established scientific construct.
propositions.resolution: The topic's construct is analytically compatible with scaffold-versus-substitute literature, but the exact term and operational definition have not been validated. It remains proposed until discriminant measures and independent review exist.

required_missing_lanes: longitudinal studies of persistent capability change
null studies showing no later performance difference
head-to-head substitution versus scaffolding interaction designs
replication across multiple LLMs, tasks, age groups, and domains
